I'm a Data Science for Political Science student at American University, spending 2026–27 on the General Course at the London School of Economics. I build cross-national panel datasets, model them in R and turn the results into charts, dashboards and writing that non-specialists can use.

My work focuses on **democratic erosion**, **comparative party politics** and **policy evaluation**. My actor-level study of democratic backsliding won its session at American University's 2026 Undergraduate Research Symposium.

## What I work with

**Methods:** fixed-effects panel models, two-part models, event studies, regression and diagnostics, text similarity

**Tools:** R (tidyverse, fixest, ggplot2, gt, tidymodels), Quarto, Git/GitHub, interactive Plotly and Observable dashboards

**Data:** V-Dem, DEED, WhoGov, Manifesto Project, DOJ FARA, General Social Survey, EIA
